prompt: When does a problem become an incident?

choices.why: An alert is a signal; nobody has taken charge yet.

choices.text: When somebody declares it and takes the role
choices.why: Right. Declared, not discovered.
That can be weeks after the incident began.
A complaint is one way to notice, not the declaration.

prompt: Unsure whether an incident is SEV2 or SEV1, which do you pick?

choices.why: Right. Lowering later is free; raising later costs the first half hour.
The people needed would join half an hour late.

choices.text: Neither until the cause is known
choices.why: Declaring waits for nothing; the cause can take hours.

choices.text: SEV3, and raise it if customers write
choices.why: That makes customers the alerting system.

prompt: Something changed 20 minutes before checkout started failing. What comes first?

choices.text: Finding the exact line that broke
choices.why: That can take an hour of failing checkouts.

choices.text: Writing the postmortem while it is fresh
choices.why: The postmortem comes after the service is back.
Right. Minutes, no diagnosis needed.

choices.text: Raising the alert's threshold so it stops firing
choices.why: That silences the evidence, not the failure.

prompt: What does the incident commander not do?
hint: Somebody has to stay above the detail.

choices.why: That is exactly the commander's call.
The commander keeps it.
Right. That is operations; the commander coordinates.
Assigning is the commander's job.

prompt: At 14:40 there is no news. What does the communications role send at the scheduled update?

choices.text: Nothing, until there is something new
choices.why: Silence reads as "nobody is working on it".

choices.text: An update saying so, with the next update's time
choices.why: Right. Four parts, no adjectives.

choices.text: A guess at the cause, to show progress
choices.why: A wrong cause in public has to be taken back.
Nobody knows it yet; a missed promise costs trust.

prompt: Why build the timeline from logs and metrics rather than from what people remember?

choices.text: Logs are required by the postmortem template
choices.why: The reason is accuracy, not a template.

choices.text: Memory orders events into the best story
choices.why: Right. Evidence keeps the order they happened in.

choices.text: People are not allowed to speak in a postmortem
choices.why: They speak; their accounts are checked against the evidence.
Only audit logs in _Required; and retention is not the point.

prompt: In the six bad minutes, 85 checkouts needed a retry and 155 went through at once. What percentage needed a retry, rounded?
Lesson 14's policy needs retries above five a minute for ten minutes. The incident lasted under six. What follows?
hint: Could the condition ever have been true?

choices.text: The policy fired four minutes after the incident ended
choices.why: It never fires: the condition needs ten minutes in a row.

choices.text: It never fired: a finding for the postmortem
choices.why: Right. Only an evidence timeline shows it.
The timeline is the evidence; the policy is what is questioned.

choices.text: Nothing: missing data counted as active
choices.why: Missing data was set to inactive, and data was not missing here.

prompt: What does a blameless postmortem ask?

choices.why: True and useless: the next person makes it too.
Right. That finding has a fix.

choices.text: How much the person should be fined
choices.why: Blame makes people hide what they did.

choices.text: Whether the incident was really an incident
choices.why: It was declared; the postmortem is about what happened.

prompt: An action item has no owner and no date. What is it?

choices.why: Without an owner it has no priority at all.
Right. Owner and date make it an action.
Nothing says so; that is the problem.
A finding is a fact about the system; this is a task without anybody.

prompt: Why does the shop's postmortem have no "root cause" heading?
hint: Slow service, short retry, long alert, a Friday.

choices.text: The cause is never known in time
choices.why: Causes are found; the question is how many.

choices.text: Root causes belong in the incident channel
choices.why: The channel records decisions, not the analysis.

choices.text: Several factors together caused it, and naming one hides the others
choices.why: Right. Contributing factors keep all of them in view.

choices.text: Blameless means no cause may be written down
choices.why: Causes are written; people are not blamed.

prompt: Which headings does the shop's postmortem have? Choose all that apply.
hint: Seven headings, one of them about luck.

choices.why: Yes.

Yes.
